matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns the abstract's claim about 1T vs 8T tokens being overstated relative to Table 5 and Figure 7 data. None of the findings identify this specific abstract-to-results inconsistency; pred_id 6 discusses Section 6 conclusions but not the abstract claim.

GT 2 identifies a mathematical inconsistency in Section 3.1's adaptive bandwidth formula (β increases but text claims bandwidth decreases). Pred_id 8 discusses bandwidth convergence in footnote 4 but addresses a different issue (dimension dependence), not the inverted relationship in Equation 6.
GT 3 concerns Table 1's suspiciously identical averages (52.2%) potentially masking cherry-picking or manipulation. No finding identifies this specific data integrity issue in Table 1.

GT 4 identifies asymmetric prompt optimization in Section 5.3 (footnote 13) where best prompts are chosen per task. No finding discusses this experimental design asymmetry or prompt selection protocol.

GT 5 concerns Section 5.2's misleading claim of 'successful extrapolation' when Table 3 shows 33-point performance drop (59.3% to 26.5%). No finding identifies this specific mischaracterization of extrapolation results.
GT 6 identifies a fabricated citation 'Zhang, 2025' with impossible year 2504 in the introduction. No finding mentions this specific citation error or the Zhang reference.

GT 7 concerns Table 2's FLOPs calculation at context length 256 concealing true computational costs at longer contexts (4k-32k). No finding identifies this specific issue with FLOPs reporting at short context.

GT 8 identifies contradiction between Appendix C's claim of no hyperparameter searching and Table 6's extensive architecture-specific learned parameters. No finding discusses this asymmetry in hyperparameter optimization claims.

GT 9 identifies Figure 3's caption overstating transformer degradation when Banking77 shows stable/modest decline. Pred_id 4 directly identifies this same figure-text inconsistency, noting the text claims 'completely fail' while the figure shows improvement from ~0.58 to ~0.70.
GT 10 concerns ethical omission in Section 4 regarding data provenance, licenses, and bias for 1T token training. No finding addresses this ethical transparency issue.

GT 11 identifies abstract's broad claim of 'significant outperformance' contradicting Section 5.1's evidence of identical performance (56.8% vs 56.6%) on 13/19 benchmarks. Pred_id 5 discusses abstract overstatement but focuses on zero-shot claims, not this specific persistent-knowledge contradiction.
GT 12 concerns excessive promotional language ('successfully scale up,' 'appealing,' 'favorable') in the introduction. No finding identifies this rhetorical manipulation issue.
GT 13 concerns Table 4's selective reporting where transformers are marked '×' at 64k without explanation. No finding identifies this specific suspicious reporting pattern in Table 4.
GT 14 identifies missing dimensionality specifications for weight matrices W_φ, W_g, W_λ in Equation 8. No finding discusses this mathematical incompleteness in the key feature extractor formulation.

GT 15 identifies Section 6's causal interpretation ignoring confounds (GQA, 8k context) when concluding data scaling is insufficient. Pred_id 6 and 7 both identify this issue: pred_id 6 notes the conclusion extends beyond evidence, and pred_id 7 specifically identifies the confounded setup with different attention types and context lengths.

GT 16 concerns Section 5.3's unjustified choice of accuracy metric over calibration-aware alternatives for classification evaluation. No finding discusses this metric selection issue or calibration concerns.

GT 17 identifies Section 2's misattribution of the associative memory-attention connection as novel when it's established background. Pred_id 3 discusses Section 3.3 footnote 8 about FFN-memory interchangeability, which is a different attribution issue.

GT 18 identifies Section 8's acknowledgment of computational cost as future work contradicting earlier claims of efficient long-context processing. No finding identifies this cross-section contradiction between discussion and earlier sections.
